taskVersion.name: ves-heldout-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station H-03, survey area H. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 193.6 | 0.90 | 0.90
2 | 129.1 | 3.18 | 4.08
3 | 29.1 | 0.79 | 4.87
4 | 29.8 | 26.64 | 31.51
5 | 165.4 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as QQA-type.

Is this label correct for these layer values? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"label_correct": true or false, "curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine the correct curve-type notation, we evaluate the resistivity values for each group of three consecutive layers:

1.  **Layers 1-2-3:** $\rho_1 = 193.6, \rho_2 = 129.1, \rho_3 = 29.1$.
    Since $193.6 > 129.1 > 29.1$ ($\rho_1 > \rho_2 > \rho_3$), the letter is **Q**.
2.  **Layers 2-3-4:** $\rho_2 = 129.1, \rho_3 = 29.1, \rho_4 = 29.8$.
    Since $129.1 > 29.1 < 29.8$ ($\rho_2 > \rho_3 < \rho_4$), the letter is **H**.
3.  **Layers 3-4-5:** $\rho_3 = 29.1, \rho_4 = 29.8, \rho_5 = 165.4$.
    Since $29.1 < 29.8 < 165.4$ ($\rho_3 < \rho_4 < \rho_5$), the letter is **A**.

Combining these letters in order, the correct sequence is **QHA**. The provided label QQA is incorrect.

{"label_correct": false, "curve_type": "QHA"}
